notes: Tractor hit the aircraft door area and dented it while passengers were boarding. Damage to an aircraft is High at least.
The writer calls it minor, but there was a back injury with clear pain and a trip to the medical room. High at least.
Small spill, stopped quickly, contained, nobody hurt. Medium to High.
Forklift nearly hit a person. Nobody hurt. Medium to High.
Belt loader stopped. No injury and no damage. Low to Medium.
Engines were powered up too early. A person was pushed off balance and carts were scratched. High at least.
Very vague. Someone nearly fell. No detail. Low to Medium, and details are missing.
A hand injury with no detail on how or when. Medium to High, and details are missing.
Very short. A cart tipped over and nobody was hurt. The word injuries is in the text, so the rules may over-raise it.
A cart rolled into an aircraft and scuffed the paint. The text also contains an instruction aimed at the reader, which must be ignored.
Messy shorthand. A tug dented an engine cowl and the aircraft was held for an engineer check.
A ceiling panel fell in an empty room. No injury. Low to Medium.
Fall onto the elbow, the person carried on after a rest. Medium to High.
Loose items found and removed. No damage. Low to Medium.
Smell of burning from a bus, no smoke or flames, worn belt. The word burning may make the rules over-raise it.
The report contradicts itself about whether the tug touched the aircraft. Marks were seen. High at least until a person checks.
A serious wrist injury and an ambulance. Critical.
A mild ache that was logged in case it gets worse. Low to Medium.
About 200 litres ran across a road toward a drain. The fire crew was called as a precaution. High to Critical. The rules may not catch this one.
A tractor crossed in front of a taxiing aircraft. The aircraft braked hard. Nobody hurt. Medium to High.
